note: Every public claim MANDATE makes must appear here with its evidence and its proof rung. A claim absent from this file may not appear in the README, the demo or the submission. NOT_CLAIMED entries exist to record what is deliberately NOT asserted. Claims marked PENDING_REPROOF were verified against a superseded registry and must be re-established before use.

supersededRegistry.reason: superseded by the lifecycle-event redeploy. Its receipts are abandoned rather than migrated, because a receipt is a commitment and moving one would defeat the point of making it.

deployments.otherReceiptsInRegistry: Five receipts exist. Three come from superseded, crashed or unregistered runs and are published with reachable evidence rather than left as unverifiable commitments. This run (20260904T155705Z) supersedes the 2026-08-19 featured mandate as the current one: the earlier run did not expire or fail, its 7-day freshness window simply closed. Its receipt and mandate remain on chain and independently verifiable; they are just no longer what this deployment features. An intermediate run on 2026-09-04 published under agent id 0 (unregistered) because the identity was not yet bound to a card at the time; it is disclosed rather than hidden and has no mandate, because the operator re-ran with the correct agent id rather than granting a session against an unregistered identity.

claims.wording: The trial result is reproducible by an independent reference model that does not share the agent's accounting implementation.
limitations: Reproducibility is asserted for the recorded observation, not for a re-fork at the original block: the fixture's block is beyond the public RPC's fork window.

claims.wording: The trial receipt is an append-only public commitment whose id recomputes from its own fields.
The evidence document served publicly is byte-identical to what the receipt committed to.

evidence.value: canonical hash of the fetched document equals the receipt's evidenceHash

claims.wording: The authority granted to the agent is no broader than the authority its trial tested, recomputed by an independent comparator from both disclosed documents.
limitations: The comparator is MANDATE's own. Its rules are published and its verdict is recomputed by the verifier rather than read from the artifact.

claims.wording: A financial action inside the granted authority executes successfully against the real protocol.
limitations: Demonstrated for Venus vUSDT repayBorrow(uint256) on chain 97.

claims.wording: An action that would take cumulative spend past the granted cap is refused by the user's own account contract, which raises ExceededSpendLimit.

evidence.value: at the attempt: cap 25000000, spent 20000000, allowance 1105000000 — the allowance is ruled out as the binding constraint

limitations: The refusal occurs before broadcast, so there is no reverted transaction. See claim rejection-produces-no-transaction.

claims.wording: The granted selector invoked on a contract outside the permission set is refused by the account contract with UnauthorizedCall.

evidence.value: canExecute returned false for the attempted target

limitations: No reverted transaction. See claim rejection-produces-no-transaction.

claims.wording: A selector outside the permission set invoked on the granted contract is refused by the account contract with UnauthorizedCall.

evidence.value: canExecute returned false for the attempted selector

limitations: No reverted transaction. See claim rejection-produces-no-transaction.

claims.wording: Revoking the session removes the key from the account and from the public KeyStore, and a previously permitted action is then refused.
The standing admin-path allowance the mandate required is disclosed as a durable effect and cleared after revocation.
limitations: Session-path approvals are force-zeroed by the account contract at the end of every batch, so the only durable approval is the admin-path one.

claims.wording: The permissions an application requests are not necessarily the permissions the chain enforces, and MANDATE displays the enforced set read from the account rather than the requested object.
Out-of-scope actions are refused during validation, before any transaction is broadcast. There is therefore no reverted transaction to inspect on an explorer.

evidence.value: every blocked attempt recorded status REVERTED with no transaction hash

limitations: MANDATE must NOT claim to show reverted transactions for blocked actions.
The evidence for a rejection is the account's state at the attempt plus the validator's error, both recorded in the evidence bundle.
This is an earlier and stronger security boundary than a reverted transaction, but it is a different artifact and must be described as one.

claims.wording: That the session was granted with these permissions, and over which window, can be reconstructed from chain after it has been revoked.

evidence.value: session registration PASS: granted over the window the activation records, revoked through the registry, both reconstructed from chain

limitations: Reconstructed from the registry's own lifecycle record rather than from account state, which no longer holds the key after revocation.

claims.wording: The mechanism has been demonstrated on BSC mainnet.
limitations: Everything demonstrated so far is BSC testnet (97). No mainnet claim may be made until a mainnet run exists.

claims.wording: The marketplace is populated with live third-party agents.
limitations: A 300-agent sample of BSC ERC-8004 registrations found ~75% bulk-mint entries from one publisher, 3.2% declaring any service, and 3 with a verified endpoint.
Inventory at launch is MANDATE reference agents. Registrations remain discoverable in search but do not enter the primary ranking.

claims.wording: MANDATE makes AI agents safe.
limitations: MANDATE bounds what a session may do. It does not make an agent correct, honest or competent.
ERC-1271 signing paths bypass both call and spend enforcement and are excluded from mandate sessions rather than defended against.

claims.wording: The party that holds the capital and the party that acts under the mandate are different keys. The owner grants the session, the agent signs every execution attempted under it, and the owner can end it without the agent's cooperation.

evidence.value: owner 0xdc5071910e6ca6855d45f96ba28ee0a2e5629299 — holds the Venus position and the wallet's admin authority
agent 0x29f7b9913dd16278db7a6cfca145953a854ca0dc — receives the session and signs the executions
agent session key 0x76de0d16e90dc68406773b79518df5fa6b491798 — derived from the agent's key and run 20260819T045553Z
publisher 0xdc5071910e6ca6855d45f96ba28ee0a2e5629299 — the owner, disclosed as such in the manifest
role-separation PASS: no two roles share an address, and the run is refused outright when they do

the activation's sessionKeyHash 0x2598f05edb7f747aba128fb23a5f3375f37f6195bc6ff7fc05d21baeaf842952 recomputes as keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(2), keccak256(abi.encode(0x76de0d16e90dc68406773b79518df5fa6b491798)))), so the agent's key is the one the account enforced against
the manifest's designationSignature recovers to the agent address, which the owner's key cannot produce, so the key that signed the executions was chosen by the agent

limitations: Both keys are currently operated by MANDATE. What is demonstrated is separation of keys and of authority, not organisational independence. See claim no-independent-agent-has-held-a-mandate.
The publisher is the owner. This is disclosed in every manifest rather than asserted to be a third party.

The agent's key holds no tBNB and none was sent to it: an Altana session is sponsored out of the wallet it acts on, so the owner paid every fee. There is therefore no owner-to-agent funding transfer in this run.
The agent signs the intent; the relay broadcasts it. The transaction sender on chain is the relay, and the account validates the agent's signature against the session key it holds.

claims.wording: A third party's agent has operated autonomously under a MANDATE-granted session.
limitations: As of run 20260819T045553Z the owner and the agent are different keys and the account enforces against the agent's: see claim owner-agent-key-separation. That closes the key-holding half of this gap and none of the trust half.
Both keys are still generated, held and run by MANDATE, from one .env and one process. A second keypair is not a second party, and this claim is about a party.
What is still NOT shown is an agent operated by someone else, on capital owned by someone else, reached over a network boundary rather than through a local signer.
The enforcement evidence is unaffected either way: the account refused the out-of-scope calls on its own, and who holds which key cannot make a refusal happen.

claims.wording: MANDATE can show an on-chain transaction for a blocked action.
limitations: The verifier's `blocked execution` step is a permanent SKIP by design. A boundary-crossing call is refused during validation and never reaches a block, so there is no transaction to fetch.
The evidence for a refusal is the `rejected intents` step, which is VERIFIED.

claims.wording: Each refused action is corroborated by the account's own state at the moment of the attempt, so the spend cap can be distinguished from an exhausted token allowance.

evidence.value: rejected intents PASS: 3 intents refused by the account before broadcast, each corroborated by the account's own state
the spend-cap intent carries allowanceAtAttemptRaw 1105000000 against amountRaw 6000000, ruling out an exhausted approval

limitations: Three of four refusals are published. The post-revoke refusal is omitted because the relay rejects a stale key before the account's validator runs, so the account raised no error to record.
